key_insight: The paper learns a multiscale stochastic dynamics model by combining spatial renormalization-group coarse graining with a path-integral time-evolution formulation, linking the predictor and score across scales.
engineering_relevance: This enables unified simulation, unconditional generation, and super-resolution for complex turbulent and multiscale flow systems.
method: Apply a stochastic RG in space using scale-dependent Laplacian damping plus additive Gaussian noise.
Formulate time evolution at each scale with an Onsager--Machlup action and optimize the drift predictor via KL divergence minimization.
Compute the score either by automatic differentiation of the path distribution or by a cheaper denoising-trained network output.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated numerically on two multiscale benchmarks: the Kolmogorov flow and the two-timescale Lorenz-96 model.
watch_item: The predictor has no closed form, so practical performance depends on neural-network approximation quality and the chosen score-estimation route.
paper_title: A Renormalization-Group Hierarchy of Stochastic Effective Dynamics Learned through Path Integrals
